To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the narratives of seven individuals with identified psychiatric diagnoses reveal common themes and plot points that are not typically associated with the diagnosis, and that these narratives can be used to inform the counseling profession about the positive qualities of individuals with identified psychiatric diagnosis.
the narratives of individuals who are diagnosed with psychiatric disorders reveal a pattern of strengths and positive qualities that are not currently being addressed by mental health professionals.

the participants in our study, all diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder, identified strengths and positive attributes that they possessed, and that these strengths and attributes were not included in the psychiatric diagnosis, and were not included in treatment plans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the narrative construction of the self in the context of a psychiatric diagnosis and its implications for counseling practice.
the identification and exploration of positive qualities inherent to psychiatric diagnoses.
the hidden strengths and the positive qualities inherent to the experience of identified psychiatric diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the seven participants were able to identify positive qualities within themselves and others that were suppressed by their diagnosis, that these qualities were not recognized or acknowledged by their mental health professionals and that they were able to identify the positive aspects of their lives and their diagnosis in a manner that would be useful to the Counseling profession.
the narratives of the Magnificent Seven were rich and full of positive and meaningful elements.

the narratives of the Magnificent Seven reveal the presence of a common theme of a struggle to maintain a sense of self, and a sense of self worth, in the face of the overwhelming and often insidious presence of a psychiatric diagnosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants’ stories are a testament to the human spirit and its ability to survive in the face of adversity.
the participants’ narratives revealed a number of strengths that were suppressed in the diagnosis, and these strengths were not only present in the past but also were evident in the current time.
the individuals we interviewed had experienced significant challenges and difficulties, but had found ways to overcome and cope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a great deal of positive, hidden strengths that can be found within a person’s story, even when that person is diagnosed as mentally ill.
the individuals we spoke to were not the sum of their psychiatric diagnoses.
there is a great deal of strength in each of these individuals, and the strength is inherent in the diagnosis.
